decisions.claim: A local process can mint its own setup link by serving one from a loopback HTTP server
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, and it defeated the entire phase in one line that I wrote for test convenience. The daemon trusted ANY https origin plus http on loopback, so a malicious agent could stand up a listener, serve a blob it encrypted with a passphrase it chose, and have every cryptographic check pass. The origin is now an allowlist read from the DAEMON's environment (default https://wundervault.com), which systemd sets and no caller can influence. Regression test stands up a real rogue server and asserts refusal.

decisions.claim: The setup link in argv is readable by same-uid agents via /proc/<pid>/cmdline
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. The link is the one credential the design assumes an agent cannot obtain, and passing it as an argument published it to every agent for the life of the command - with time to redeem it first, since GET and burn are separate. The link is now read from stdin; piping still works, so it stays scriptable.

decisions.claim: Burning is not atomic with enrolment: it happens before validation and persistence, and failures are ignored
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. redeemSetupLink burned the link before the socket token was checked and before the profile was stored, so a missing token or a disk error spent a single-use link and produced no agent. The burn is now handed back to the caller and invoked only after registerProfile succeeds; the socket token is validated before anything is redeemed.

decisions.claim: Migration replaces the per-agent token, contradicting spec F3
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED and a real operational break: an agent process reads its token at startup, so a fresh token locks it out of a daemon that had just enrolled it, with 'unauthorized' as the only clue. Enrolment now restores the existing token when one is present, via a new set_socket_token action authorised by the token just set. Spec F3 updated to say PRESERVE rather than merely stay.

decisions.claim: The mgmt data handler can re-run the same enrol request on every data event
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED - the handler reparses the buffer on each chunk and the enrol path returns early without marking the connection consumed. A caller could send one valid line then dribble bytes, stacking 100,000-round PBKDF2 operations and fetches on the event loop every agent's credential socket shares. One request per connection now, with a test that counts server hits.

decisions.claim: Migration shreds the old store without requiring the old unit to be stopped, and cannot be repaired by rerunning
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED as a regression I introduced when rewriting migrate.ts - the conditional shred from round 12 was lost. Kept the shred deliberately (reaching --finish means every agent was repaired, so those credentials are already dead server-side: stale ciphertext, not a live secret) but the real gap was the unit FILE surviving to restart at boot. It is now removed, and a still-running unit is reported rather than glossed.

decisions.claim: --destinations has no dispatch path in wundervault-agent
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. It was only ever wired into the wundervault-mcp binary, while the daemon's help text, the log viewer's error and the mgmt socket's refusal all tell people to run 'sudo wundervault-agent --destinations' - which fell through to the daemon branch and died in refuseRoot. Now dispatched in agent.ts, and deliberately NOT subject to refuseRoot, since reading the store is the one thing that requires being root.
